original_question: On which chromosome is the gene associated with Carey-Fineman-Ziter syndrome, which also plays a role in myoblast fusion?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene associated with Carey-Fineman-Ziter syndrome, which also plays a role in myoblast fusion?
final_qi.long_answer: Carey-Fineman-Ziter syndrome is caused by recessive mutations in the MYMK gene (also called myomaker), a membrane protein required for myoblast fusion during skeletal-muscle development. The human MYMK locus is situated on chromosome 9 (cytogenetic band 9q34), establishing chromosome 9 as the chromosomal location linked to the disorder.
